newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees sugar price boost in liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees sugar price boost in liberalisation.

text.p: World sugar prices would increase substantially if the United States alone were to introduce full liberalisation of its sugar sector, Harry Bonanno, chairman of Australia's peak canegrowers body CANEGROWERS, said on Tuesday.

In a statement from Copenhagen, Bonanno said he would press the World Association of Beet and Cane Growers (WABCG) in Copenhagen on Tuesday for governments in Europe and the U.S. to demonstrate a commitment to genuine trade liberalisation.
The conference was held at a crucial time in the development of the sugar industry in the Australian state of Queensland, he said.
Bonanno, who is also vice president of WABCG, said efficient sugar producing countries such as Australia could expect significant benefits from greater trade liberalisation of the world market.

Australian growers were keen to improve market access conditions and provide a more predictable trading environment for an industry traditionally plagued by volatile prices and high levels of price corruption from national policies, he said.
Australian cane growers faced serious threats from increasing efficiency in other sugar-producing countries and the rapid rise in market share by artificial sweeteners, he said.
